mesa: Methylation Enrichment Sequencing Analysis

Source: R/mesa-package.R
mesa-package.Rd

mesa analyses DNA methylation measured by enrichment sequencing, such as MeDIP-seq (methylated DNA immunoprecipitation) and MBD-seq (methyl-CpG binding domain capture), including low-input samples such as cell-free DNA. These assays pull down methylated fragments instead of converting unmethylated cytosines, so the signal is a read count per genomic window whose relation to methylation depends on the local CpG density. mesa builds on the qseaSet class from qsea, which models that relation, and adds functions to build, quality-control, explore and compare qseaSet objects in a tidyverse style.

Workflow

A typical analysis follows these steps:

  1. Build a qseaSet from BAM files with makeQset(), which tiles the genome into windows, counts fragments and estimates copy number (see addHMMcopyCNV()). addNormalisation() fits the CpG-density-dependent enrichment used to estimate beta values.

  2. Check quality with getSampleQCSummary() and plotCorrelationMatrix(), and subset samples or windows with filter(), filterWindows() or subsetQset().

  3. Explore sample structure with principal components (getPCA()) or UMAP (getUMAP()).

  4. Compare groups of samples with calculateDMRs(), which fits a negative binomial model per window and returns differentially methylated regions (DMRs), and summarise them with summariseDMRsByContrast().

  5. Extract counts, normalised reads per million (nrpm) or beta values per window with getDataTable(), for example over the DMRs after filterByOverlaps().

  6. Annotate windows or DMRs with nearby genes and genomic features with annotateWindows() and plotGenomicFeatureDistribution().

Two small qseaSet objects are shipped for examples: exampleTumourNormal (human, paired tumour/normal samples) and exampleMouse (mouse cell line).

Examples

# A qseaSet of 10 samples (5 tumour/normal pairs) over windows on chr7
exampleTumourNormal
#> qseaSet
#> =======================================
#> 10 Samples: 
#> Colon1_N, Colon1_T, Colon2_N, Colon2_T, Lung1_N, Lung1_T, Lung2_N, Lung2_T, Lung3_N, Lung3_T
#> 819 Regions in 22 chromosomes of BSgenome.Hsapiens.NCBI.GRCh38
getSampleTable(exampleTumourNormal)
#>          sample_name    group patient        type tumour tissue age gender
#> Colon1_N    Colon1_N Colon1_N  Colon1 NormalColon Normal  Colon  80      F
#> Colon1_T    Colon1_T Colon1_T  Colon1         CRC Tumour  Colon  80      F
#> Colon2_N    Colon2_N Colon2_N  Colon2 NormalColon Normal  Colon  67      F
#> Colon2_T    Colon2_T Colon2_T  Colon2         CRC Tumour  Colon  67      F
#> Lung1_N      Lung1_N  Lung1_N   Lung1  NormalLung Normal   Lung  64      F
#> Lung1_T      Lung1_T  Lung1_T   Lung1        LUAD Tumour   Lung  64      F
#> Lung2_N      Lung2_N  Lung2_N   Lung2  NormalLung Normal   Lung  71      F
#> Lung2_T      Lung2_T  Lung2_T   Lung2        LUSC Tumour   Lung  71      F
#> Lung3_N      Lung3_N  Lung3_N   Lung3  NormalLung Normal   Lung  72      M
#> Lung3_T      Lung3_T  Lung3_T   Lung3        LUAD Tumour   Lung  72      M
#>          stage
#> Colon1_N  <NA>
#> Colon1_T   III
#> Colon2_N  <NA>
#> Colon2_T    IV
#> Lung1_N   <NA>
#> Lung1_T    IIA
#> Lung2_N   <NA>
#> Lung2_T     IA
#> Lung3_N   <NA>
#> Lung3_T     IB

# Beta values (methylation estimates) per window and sample
exampleTumourNormal %>%
    getDataTable(normMethod = "beta") %>%
    head()
#> Generating table of beta values for 819 regions across 10 samples.
#> # A tibble: 6 × 14
#>   seqnames  start    end CpG_density Colon1_N Colon1_T Colon2_N Colon2_T Lung1_N

#> 2 7        2.50e7 2.50e7       13.4    0.0565   0.0171   0.0275   0.0165  0.0171
#> 3 7        2.50e7 2.50e7        5.57  NA        0.204   NA        0.363   0.353 
#> 4 7        2.50e7 2.50e7        5.10  NA        0.382   NA        0.406   0.393 
#> 5 7        2.50e7 2.50e7        8.38   0.122    0.0695   0.918    0.818   0.901 
#> 6 7        2.50e7 2.50e7       17.9    0.0240   0.0660   0.265    0.250   0.161 
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: Lung1_T <dbl>, Lung2_N <dbl>, Lung2_T <dbl>,
#> #   Lung3_N <dbl>, Lung3_T <dbl>

# Differentially methylated regions between tumour and normal samples
exampleTumourNormal %>%
    calculateDMRs(variable = "tumour", contrasts = "first") %>%
    head()
